summary: A 2–6 m many-stemmed shrub with flexible flood-bent shoots and adventitious roots. It colonizes freshwater riverbanks and gravel bars, but dependable seasonal fruiting is restricted to mapped low spring-fed reaches whose roots retain year-round groundwater access. Increasing spring day length and temperature cue flowering; water, light, nutrients and pollination determine the eventual crop. Fruit draws rondo and dense stems conceal merodeador (F11, F18, F21).

links: Runoff alternately buries and exposes channel-side stems.
Buried living nodes root in damp sediment.
Root networks retain gravel and support recovery after partial damage.
chains.play: Follow thickets along freshwater corridors and gather fallen flexible stems.
chains.weakness: Scour removes root mats; prolonged burial or submergence kills shoots, and disconnected bars can dry out.
observe: New roots emerge from buried nodes.
Gravel collects downstream of stem clusters.
Bent survivors produce upright shoots after floods.

plausibility.judge: strict review: sol (codex) + DeepSeek; chair sol
plausibility.summary: Flood regeneration permits colonization of seasonal gravel bars without guaranteeing permanent water access or fruit. Marine tides are not the driver. Strict review (2026-11-19): Residual: Flexibility, rooting of buried nodes and recovery after partial damage form a coherent freshwater disturbance strategy. Residual weakness: neither flexibility nor roots prevent uprooting during severe scour, and sediment retention depends on establishment before a flood. F8 supplies storms and F18 supplies seasonal drying; neither specifies local discharge.

analogues.mechanism: Flexible shoots, regeneration and adventitious rooting interact with freshwater flow and sediment deposition.

chains.trait: Seasonally cued fruit on perennial spring-fed reaches
links: Increasing day length and suitable temperatures during spring cue flowering in reproductively ready shrubs (F11).
Adequate light, nutrients and pollination permit fruit set.
On mapped low spring-fed reaches, year-round root access to groundwater reduces fruit abortion during summer drying (F18, F21).
Soft seasonal fruit rewards rondo with water and carbohydrates.
Some hard-coated seeds survive fruit feeding and transport, a proposed trait of this shrub.
chains.play: Seek late-summer to autumn fruit on mapped perennial spring-fed reaches, while checking for an actual crop rather than treating water access as a guarantee.
chains.weakness: Groundwater disconnection, insufficient light or nutrients, failed pollination and unsuitable deposition sites interrupt reproduction.
observe: Flower buds open as spring days lengthen and temperatures rise.
Soft green-gold fruit later hangs over a mapped perennial spring-fed channel.
Rondo leaves some intact seeds on moist openings beyond the thicket.

plausibility.judge: strict review: sol (codex) + DeepSeek; chair sol
plausibility.summary: Enable regular fruit production only where roots retain year-round groundwater connection. Water access permits a crop but does not guarantee one; softness and scent indicate ripeness. Strict review (2026-11-19): revised: The chain lacked a seasonal cue and overextended groundwater evidence, so spring phenology and conditional fruiting now operate only on mapped perennial spring-fed reaches. Still open: The pivotal link is unsupported by its roots. F21 describes one dyke-dammed spring at the giant tree, not a network of perennial reach-scale aquifers, and F18 only establishes summer drying; 'mapped low spring-fed reaches' is an extrapolation. 'Adequate light, nutrients and pollination permit fruit set' is a tautology, no pollen vector is named, and 'reproductively ready' makes the F11 photoperiod link unfalsifiable.

analogues.mechanism: Seasonal flowering cues and resource supply constrain fruit production, while animal transport and suitable deposition constrain recruitment; exact cues and seed survival are proposed species traits.

gameplay.gift_item: Soft river-fruit cluster from a groundwater-connected thicket

poison.signal: Green foliage; softness and scent identify ripe fruit.

gameplay.cover: Dense stems conceal small creatures and predators.
gameplay.nest_material: Fallen flexible twigs, bark fibres and leaves.
gameplay.notes: Only year-round groundwater-connected patches support regular seasonal fruiting. Fruit does not cure poisoning, shrub presence does not certify potable water, and slender stems do not reliably bear player weight.

relations.note: Visits fruiting groundwater-connected patches and transports some surviving seeds.
On fog-damp meadow reaches, forages for soft grasses and associated aquatic greens along adjacent open freshwater margins.
Conceals approaches to crossings and fruit visitors.
Forms shrub ribbons through meadow channels, including some seasonal nonfruiting bars.
Shelters ferns in persistently humid bank pockets.
Provides craft material throughout suitable thickets and fruit only in eligible patches.

generator.trunk: Several slender woody stems from a shared crown; old stems arch over deposited gravel.

branching.buttress: Absent; root mats and rooted low branches form the base.

colour.base: Medium green leaves and olive-brown stems
overlay_rules: Eligible ripe fruit becomes soft muted green-gold.
Red is not a fruit-edibility cue.

placement.slope: Freshwater channel margins, moist gravel bars and spring-fed benches.
placement.wetness: Moist rooting sediment permits establishment; regular fruiting additionally requires mapped perennial groundwater access.
placement.density: Bank ribbons and bar colonies interrupted by scour.

constraints.hydrology_validation: Reject marine or brackish influence using mapped local tidal reach and root-zone water, regardless of coast distance.

fruiting.site_requirement: Explicitly mapped low spring-fed reach with year-round root-zone groundwater connection; F21 supports the spring outflow.
fruiting.flowering_cue: Increasing spring day length and suitable temperature in a reproductively ready shrub.
fruiting.water_rule: Perennial groundwater is necessary for dependable crops but does not guarantee fruit set or maturation.

generator.seasonal: Wet periods support growth and resprouting. Spring flowering can produce late-summer to autumn fruit at eligible perennial spring-fed sites; seasonal gravel-bar colonies remain unreliable fruit sources.
generator.wind_response: Slender stems bow together; floods leave persistent downstream bends.

journal.en: The river bends it and buries it. Fruit stays where its roots keep the water.
journal.es: El río la dobla y la entierra. El fruto queda donde las raíces conservan el agua.

strict second review (sol + DeepSeek) applied by sol: The plausible flood-regeneration chain remains unchanged.; F24 was removed from the revised fruit chain because shared biochemistry does not establish seed dispersal or water requirements.; Spring lengthening and warming provide the seasonal cue; the suggested phrase 'after the dry season' was not adopted because the established summer drought precedes shortening autumn days.
